Title: Pruning tips? Organic basil plant I purchased May 2019

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: an unpinched basil that grew into one tall stem.** Basil left alone sends its energy into a single growing tip, so the plant stretches upward and the lower stem bares off. Your photo fits that: a long bare stalk with the leafy growth clustered at the top right. Two other possibilities:

- **Normal aging.** An older plant that drops its lower leaves and keeps dense growth at the top is behaving normally, per [Blooming Expert](https://www.bloomingexpert.com/tips/leggy-growth/). Since the leafy top looks healthy, this may also be part of the picture.
- **Too little light.** Stems that lean toward a window, with long gaps between pale leaves, point to light. Your photo doesn't clearly show that, but check it. Pruning alone won't fix it. [Urban Harvest Lab](https://urbanharvestlab.com/blog/plant-problems/leggy-basil-indoors-light-or-pruning/) notes that a stretched plant will just grow another spindly stem if the light stays weak.

**Fix:**

1. **Cut the woody stalk back.** Remove it just above the lowest node that still has leaves, angled slightly. Don't cut into bare wood with no leaves below the cut, because it may not regrow. Basil can regrow after pruning, but not if you cut all the way to the ground, per [Get Busy Gardening](https://getbusygardening.com/pruning-basil/).
2. **Pinch every 2 to 3 weeks.** Snap off the growing tip just above a leaf pair each time a stem reaches about 6 to 8 inches. Pinch any flower buds right away.
3. **Give it a bright spot.** Aim for 6 to 8 hours of direct sun, or a grow light for 10 to 12 hours if your window is weak.
4. **Hold fertilizer for about 6 weeks** after pruning and recent repotting, since too much feeding produces soft, floppy growth.

Because you recently repotted, water only when the top inch of soil is dry, and make sure the pot drains. Your two seedlings can stay, but thin them or move one to its own pot so they don't compete.
